metadata.archetype_justification: MongoDB read queries dominate the GET /rates endpoint (the primary API surface); POST /quote is stateless computation with no database writes. No write operations to any data store. Classified as data-gateway.

findings.title: Managed Compute — Containerized but cluster unconfirmed
findings.description: The application has been containerized with a multi-stage Dockerfile and full Kubernetes manifests (Deployment with 2 replicas, Service, ConfigMap, Namespace). However, no IaC defines the underlying cluster, and the README states the legacy deployment model is a single EC2 instance with forever.
findings.gap: Containerization artifacts exist but no IaC confirms the workload runs on managed container orchestration (EKS/ECS/Fargate). Legacy EC2 deployment model documented in README.
findings.recommendation: Define the EKS cluster (or ECS service) in IaC (Terraform/CDK) and deploy the existing K8s manifests to a managed cluster.

findings.title: Managed Databases — Self-managed MongoDB on bare IP
findings.description: MongoDB is entirely self-managed. The source code connects to mongodb://10.0.8.20:27017/shipping (a bare IP address). The K8s ConfigMap references mongodb://mongo-service:27017/shipping indicating a self-managed MongoDB deployed as a Kubernetes service. No managed database resource exists.
findings.gap: All database infrastructure is self-managed with no automated failover, no managed patching, no encryption, and no authentication configured.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible) for a managed, encrypted, Multi-AZ document database. Use AWS DMS for data replication during migration.

findings.title: Network Security — No network configuration
findings.description: No VPC, subnet, security group, or network policy configuration exists. MongoDB binds to 0.0.0.0 with no authentication. The K8s Service is ClusterIP but no network policies restrict pod-to-pod traffic.
findings.gap: No network security configuration. MongoDB exposed without authentication on all interfaces. No network policies in K8s manifests.
findings.recommendation: Add Kubernetes NetworkPolicy resources to restrict ingress/egress. Deploy the database in a private subnet with security groups. Enable MongoDB authentication immediately.

findings.title: API Entry Point — No gateway or load balancer
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront configured. The K8s Service is ClusterIP with no Ingress resource active. A commented-out Ingress with ALB annotations exists but is not implemented.
findings.gap: No managed entry point with throttling, auth, or request validation.
findings.recommendation: Activate the commented-out ALB Ingress resource or configure an API Gateway (HTTP API) in front of the service.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling — Static capacity
findings.description: No auto-scaling configured. The K8s Deployment uses static replicas: 2 with no Horizontal Pod Autoscaler. All capacity is statically provisioned.
findings.gap: No auto-scaling — cannot respond to traffic spikes or scale down during low demand.
findings.recommendation: Add a Kubernetes HPA targeting CPU/memory utilization or custom metrics.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery — No backups configured
findings.description: No backup configuration found for the MongoDB data store. No automated backup, no PITR, no backup destination.
findings.gap: No automated backups for the primary data store. A data loss event would be unrecoverable.
findings.recommendation: Migrating to Amazon DocumentDB provides automated backups. In the interim, implement automated mongodump to S3.

findings.title: High Availability — No multi-AZ configuration
findings.description: No multi-AZ configuration found. K8s Deployment has 2 replicas but no pod anti-affinity or topology spread constraints. MongoDB is a single instance on one IP address.
findings.gap: Single point of failure on database; no guaranteed AZ distribution for compute pods.
findings.recommendation: Add topology spread constraints to K8s Deployment. Migrate MongoDB to DocumentDB with Multi-AZ enabled.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code — Partial coverage (K8s only)
findings.description: Kubernetes manifests define the compute deployment layer (Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Namespace). However, no IaC exists for database, networking, cluster provisioning, monitoring, or operational resources. Coverage ~20%.
findings.gap: Database, networking, cluster provisioning, monitoring, and operational resources have no IaC.
findings.recommendation: Expand IaC using Terraform or CDK to define EKS cluster, DocumentDB, VPC/networking, CloudWatch alarms, and Secrets Manager.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — No pipeline exists
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. No GitHub Actions, buildspec.yml, Jenkinsfile, or CodePipeline definitions. Deployment is manual: git pull + forever restart over SSH.
findings.gap: All deployments are manual with no automated build, test, or deploy stages.
findings.recommendation: Implement a CI/CD pipeline with stages: lint → test → build Docker image → push to ECR → deploy to EKS with automated rollback.

findings.title: Programming Languages — Compound legacy stack
findings.description: Node.js 0.10.x (EOL 2016) with Express 3.4.8 (EOL) and mongodb driver 1.4.7 (EOL). All three axes are severely outdated. No AWS SDK present.
findings.gap: Language version, framework, and driver all severely outdated (8-10+ years past EOL).
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Node.js 20+ with Express 4.x/5.x, mongodb driver 6.x, and add AWS SDK v3.

findings.title: API Versioning — No versioning strategy
findings.description: No API versioning strategy exists. Endpoints are /rates and /quote with no version prefix, no headers, no versioning annotations.
findings.gap: No versioning — any API change affects all consumers simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-path versioning (e.g., /v1/rates, /v1/quote).

findings.title: Service Discovery — Environment variable configuration
findings.description: MongoDB endpoint hardcoded in source (10.0.8.20:27017). K8s ConfigMap externalizes to K8s DNS (mongo-service:27017). Service itself discoverable via K8s Service DNS. Basic externalization but no dynamic discovery.
findings.gap: Source code hardcodes MongoDB IP. K8s provides basic DNS but no dynamic service discovery mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Remove hardcoded URLs from source. Consider AWS Cloud Map or service mesh for dynamic discovery.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage — No managed object storage
findings.description: No S3 or managed object storage found. Rate data stored in self-managed MongoDB. No Textract or document processing. Data accessible only via self-managed MongoDB.
findings.gap: No managed object storage. Data locked in self-managed MongoDB with no S3 integration or broader data accessibility.
findings.recommendation: Export reference rate data to S3 for analytics access and backup during managed database migration.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer — Inline database access
findings.description: No data access layer exists. MongoClient.connect opened per-request directly inside the route handler. No repository pattern, no DAO, no connection pooling.
findings.gap: Database access inline in route handlers with no abstraction. Per-request connection opening (no pool).
findings.recommendation: Extract database operations into a dedicated data access module. Implement connection pooling.

findings.title: Database Engine Version — MongoDB 2.4 (10+ years past EOL)
findings.description: MongoDB 2.4 referenced in README — EOL since 2016. The mongodb Node.js driver is version 1.4.7 (2014). No version pinning in IaC. Known security vulnerabilities, no modern features.
findings.gap: Database engine 10+ years past EOL with known vulnerabilities and no vendor support.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon DocumentDB (MongoDB 5.0+ compatible) or upgrade to MongoDB 7.x.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest — No encryption configured
findings.description: No encryption at rest configured for MongoDB. MongoDB 2.4 predates native encryption (introduced in 3.2 Enterprise). No KMS keys or encryption configuration exists.
findings.gap: Data at rest completely unprotected. MongoDB 2.4 does not support native encryption.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to DocumentDB (encryption at rest with KMS by default). Interim: upgrade MongoDB to 4.0+ with encryption.

findings.title: API Authentication — Static shared API key
findings.description: Static shared API key checked via x-api-key header. Not token-based (no OAuth2/JWT). No per-client identity, no expiration, no rotation.
findings.gap: Static API key without token-based auth. No per-client identity or rotation capability.
findings.recommendation: Implement JWT-based authentication via API Gateway authorizer or Cognito.

findings.title: Centralized Identity — No IdP integration
findings.description: No integration with any centralized identity provider. Self-managed static API key is the only auth mechanism. No Cognito, OIDC, or SAML.
findings.gap: Application manages its own authentication entirely with no external IdP integration.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito or organizational IdP for centralized authentication.

findings.title: Secrets Management — Plaintext credentials in source
findings.description: Plaintext credentials hardcoded in source: API_KEY = 'ship-2013-abc123-static' and MONGO_URL = 'mongodb://10.0.8.20:27017/shipping'. K8s deployment improves with secretKeyRef but source code still contains plaintext values.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in source code committed to version control. Deployment-blocking security issue.
findings.recommendation: Remove all hardcoded credentials from source. Use environment variables at runtime. Migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with rotation. Rotate exposed credentials.

findings.title: Compute Hardening — Hardened runtime, no patching
findings.description: Container runtime well-hardened: non-root user, read-only filesystem, all capabilities dropped, Alpine base. No automated patching strategy or vulnerability scanning.
findings.gap: Good runtime hardening but no patching automation and no vulnerability scanning.
findings.recommendation: Add container image scanning (ECR/Trivy) to CI/CD. Implement automated base image rebuild triggers.

findings.title: Security Pipeline — No scanning configured
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured. No CI/CD pipeline exists. No Dependabot, no SAST, no container scanning, no npm audit. Known CVEs in dependencies undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning of any kind. Known CVEs in dependencies unaddressed.
findings.recommendation: Include npm audit, ECR image scanning, and SAST (Semgrep) in CI/CD pipeline. Add Dependabot for automated updates.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — No instrumentation
findings.description: No distributed tracing instrumented. No OpenTelemetry, X-Ray, or trace ID propagation. No tracing library in dependencies.
findings.gap: No tracing — debugging request flows across service boundaries is impossible.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry SDK (Node.js auto-instrumentation) with X-Ray or OTLP collector backend.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — No SLOs or monitoring
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no latency or error rate monitoring, no availability targets. No monitoring configuration exists.
findings.gap: No SLOs or monitoring — cannot measure whether service meets user expectations.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for rate lookup latency (p99) and availability. Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics — No custom metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No CloudWatch metrics, no StatsD, no Prometheus endpoint. Only console.log at startup.
findings.gap: No business metrics — cannot track service value delivery or usage patterns.
findings.recommendation: Instrument business metrics: rate lookups by origin/dest, quote volume, error rates by endpoint.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection — No alerting configured
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no PagerDuty integration. Failures go undetected.
findings.gap: No alerting — failures and degradation go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms on error rate, latency p99, and database connection failures.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy — Rolling update only
findings.description: K8s Deployment uses default RollingUpdate with readiness/liveness probes. No canary, no blue/green, no traffic shifting, no automated rollback beyond K8s default.
findings.gap: Rolling update only — regressions affect all replicas before detection.
findings.recommendation: Implement canary deployments using Argo Rollouts or Flagger with progressive traffic shifting.

findings.title: Integration Testing — No tests exist
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. No unit tests, no integration tests, no API contract tests. README confirms 'No tests; no linting.'
findings.gap: Zero test coverage — any code change carries full regression risk.
findings.recommendation: Add integration tests for GET /rates and POST /quote using Jest with testcontainers for MongoDB.

findings.title: Incident Response — No runbooks
findings.description: No runbooks, no automation documents, no self-healing patterns. Incident response entirely ad hoc.
findings.gap: No incident response procedures — operators have no documented guidance.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for common failure modes: MongoDB connection failures, high error rate, pod crash loops.

findings.title: Observability Ownership — No ownership defined
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS, no dashboards, no alarms with named owners, no team attribution. No observability assets exist to own.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — no dashboards, no alarms, no team accountability.
findings.recommendation: Establish observability ownership after implementing metrics and alerting (OPS-Q3, OPS-Q4).

findings.title: Resource Tagging — K8s labels only
findings.description: Kubernetes labels consistently applied (app.kubernetes.io convention) across all manifests. No AWS resource tags (no IaC). No cost allocation or ownership tags.
findings.gap: K8s labels consistent but limited. No cost allocation, ownership, or environment tagging on AWS resources.
findings.recommendation: Implement a tagging standard using Terraform default_tags when expanding IaC. Add environment/team labels to K8s manifests.

evaluations.title: Workflow Orchestration
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — no multi-step workflows exist in this data-gateway's read path. Correct by design.

evaluations.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — synchronous reads dominate and are the correct design for a data-gateway archetype. No write-back or indexing flows exist.

evaluations.title: Monolith vs Microservices
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — small, focused microservice with single responsibility (shipping rates), independently deployable with well-defined boundaries.

evaluations.title: Async vs Sync Communication
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — synchronous reads are the correct pattern for this data-gateway. No downstream service calls, no write-back flows.

evaluations.title: Long-Running Process Handling
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — no operations exceed 30 seconds. Simple DB lookup and arithmetic computation only.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — no stored procedures or proprietary SQL. MongoDB NoSQL with all business logic in application layer.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false. This application repo contains no AWS resource provisioning IaC. CloudTrail evaluation belongs in the account/foundation infrastructure repo.
